# An Agent-Oriented Game-Development Product Direction

> [↑ Back to the agent-friendliness study](README.en.md)

Research date: 2026-09-18. This page separates existing capabilities, external research, and product proposals. It contains no measured Origo game-generation success rate or market-validation result.

## Distinguish two user tasks

**Framework maintenance** changes Origo's C# interfaces, lifecycle, persistence, or Godot bridge and passes repository CI. **Building games with the framework** implements gameplay, scenes, UI, assets, and delivery in a Godot.NET consumer project. Both require API understanding, but their deliverables differ: passing framework tests does not establish a playable game.

Origo is a game framework with an engine-independent Core and a Godot adapter, rather than a complete engine. It organizes state, strategies, entities, sessions, and persistence. Godot supplies rendering, the editor, physics, input, and asset import.[Architecture overview](../overview.en.md), [adapter responsibilities](../../Origo.GodotAdapter/README.en.md)

## Actual game-development evaluations

| Primary-source evaluation | Verified scope | Limits for Origo |
|---|---|---|
| [GameDevBench repository](https://github.com/waynchi/gamedevbench), first paper 2026-02 | Current README lists 333 localized Godot development tasks across graphics, animation, UI, and logic; exact Godot 4.4.1 required. Public runner and validation; Apache-2.0.[License](https://github.com/waynchi/gamedevbench/blob/main/LICENSE) | [Paper v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11103v1) contains 132 tasks: never mix versions or results. This is neither an Origo C# suite nor complete game delivery. Ported tasks must be labeled a derived evaluation. |
| [GameCraft-Bench](https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/gamecraft-bench), paper 2026-06-16 | 140 tasks in 15 families; submissions include complete Godot projects and replayable inputs, graded through interaction evidence and hidden rubrics. Public Apache-2.0 repository; current installation pins Godot 4.6.2, Ubuntu 22.04, Xvfb/xdotool/ffmpeg.[Protocol and execution](https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/gamecraft-bench#evaluation-protocol), [license](https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/gamecraft-bench/blob/main/LICENSE) | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.17861v1) and current repository rankings describe different dates; do not combine results. Its existing environment downloads standard Godot. Origo requires a separately pinned .NET engine, SDK, and framework; direct support cannot be claimed. |
| [JAMER / JamBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19830), first version 2026-06-18, revised 06-21 | Paper describes 300 projects for theme-driven generation/completion, using Godot 4.x, GDScript 2.0, compilation, structural completeness, and behavioral alignment.[Task protocol](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.19830v1) | Evaluates game code frameworks with placeholder assets, not complete artwork or playable quality. This search did not verify a downloadable full release and consolidated dataset license. Verify these before running; the abstract's openness statement alone does not establish reproducibility. |

GameDevBench incurs inference, image/video, and display-environment costs; official strict Linux execution requires Bubblewrap, Xvfb, and related tools.[Requirements](https://github.com/waynchi/gamedevbench#platform-notes) GameCraft-Bench adds recording, replay, and multimodal judging costs; it reports tokens instead of a universal dollar price, and assets have separate licenses.[Cost and asset guidance](https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/gamecraft-bench#token-usage) Budget estimation should begin with reference and empty submissions, then a small sample. Unsupported claims of negligible per-task cost are inappropriate. Gameplay-agent wins, rewards, or navigation scores cannot substitute for development-artifact acceptance.

## Origo's existing foundation and gaps

The [SND quick start](../../usage/quick-start.en.md) already documents `HealthInitStrategy`, `SndMetaFluentBuilder`, `ctx.Template.CloneTemplate`, and `entity.OwningSession.Spawn`, connecting state definition, strategy, template, and execution. `OrigoDefaultEntry.Bootstrap.cs` actually calls `ConfigureStrategies` before `sndContext.Bootstrap()`; exceptions invoke `MarkBootstrapFailed` and are rethrown. Agents should use this public startup path, without manually stitching low-level initialization.[Startup contracts](../../Origo.GodotAdapter/Bootstrap/README.en.md)

The [strategy harness](../../usage/strategy-testing.en.md) isolates data, lifecycle, and save requests, without validating real nodes, multiple entities, or full Godot scenes. [Integration tests](../../Origo.GodotAdapter.Integration.Tests/README.en.md) add real-engine behavior. The console's `tree_debug` exposes scene structure, `press_button` directly emits `Pressed`, and `camera_view` reports projection coordinates. The latter two cannot establish mouse hit testing, unobstructed UI, correct focus, or acceptable rendered output.[Console contracts](../../Origo.GodotAdapter/Console/README.en.md)

Inference: these foundations justify piloting agent workflows for small games with substantial state and persistence. They do not establish superiority over direct Godot, or the generated project's enjoyment, performance, or commercial readiness. Add real GUI replay and visual evidence to game acceptance; this does not require placing screenshot infrastructure inside Core.

## Proposed roadmap and falsifiable user experiment

1. **Start with a runnable entry.** Provide a Godot.NET consumer starter and a few complete examples: collection/scoring, failure/restart, and save recovery. Pin licensed assets, scene paths, template maps, and entry configuration. A fresh conversation and directory should complete build, launch, real input, and save recovery. This is a proposal, not implemented by this investigation.
2. **Shorten task routes.** Offer task-specific recipes and contracts for strategies, entity spawning, UI binding, and save/load. Errors should identify the violated contract and relevant documentation. Route maintainers and consumers to appropriate instructions while preserving one access path and avoiding duplicated low-level APIs.
3. **Establish two verification layers.** Core/strategy tests check rules; actual Godot.NET execution, input replay, screenshots, and video check the experience. Calibrate environments before the [fixed-budget A/B protocol](benchmarks.en.md). Distinguish script/SDK host conditions from product contracts; one machine's bootstrap failure cannot establish universal user failure.
4. **Validate value before expansion.** Recruit 12–20 Godot C# developers, stratify by experience, and use randomized crossover tasks with matched difficulty but different content. First compare current Origo materials with the candidate agent package. Separately compare Origo against direct Godot, recording design and documentation differences. Fix model, harness, time, and human-rescue permissions; grade artifacts blindly.

The direct-Godot condition should use identical Godot.NET and C# versions, assets, initial content, and acceptance rules. Prompts describe player-observable requirements, such as collecting items to increase a score and restoring it after restarting; they must not require SND, Strategy, or Session APIs. The Origo condition chooses public framework capabilities, while the Godot condition uses normal scenes and nodes. Report framework setup, feature implementation, and ongoing maintenance separately. Do not select only tasks already covered by Origo modules. Stratify by target genre, retain input/rendering-heavy tasks that may disadvantage Origo, and have independent reviewers inspect starters and prompts for answer leakage or asymmetric preimplementation.
Preregister the hypothesis: the candidate package reduces median time to the first playable loop by at least 20%, increases completion without human repair, and introduces no increase in persistence/lifecycle defects. Report failures and confidence intervals. Missing the threshold rejects that version's value hypothesis and motivates improving entry paths or narrowing target genres. Follow with a second task after one week and voluntary continued use, interviewing participants who leave. A small sample supports pilot value only, not market popularity. Expand genres, asset workflows, and editor tools only after sustained evidence.

## Long-term direction: observation, action, and feedback

A proposed long-term product direction is a stable **observation–action–feedback contract**. Observation combines auditable game state with images identified by time and scene. Actions use the existing single public capability path or actual input, stating preconditions and failure reasons. Feedback includes artifact changes, state assertions, input replay, and visual evidence. State checks and player experience complement each other: emitting a signal cannot establish actual input reachability, and screenshots cannot establish save integrity. This is a capability to design, not an existing unified tool contract.

First validate state/persistence-heavy genres such as turn-based strategy, management, branching narrative, and lightweight games with persistent progression. Their suitability is inferred from Origo's responsibilities and still requires task and user experiments. Trace assets and scenes to their sources, licenses, import parameters, template/scene mappings, and current artifact hashes so agents can distinguish code, resource, and scene-wiring failures.

Interoperability across agents should share verifiable input/output schemas, error semantics, permission boundaries, and evidence formats. Different harnesses should be able to inspect the same project and audit artifacts without depending on one vendor's prompt habits. People continue to decide aesthetics, enjoyment, pacing, genre positioning, and release tradeoffs; automated checks validate expressible contracts and evidence. Long-term success means developers repeatedly completing real tasks and choosing to retain and maintain the results. This direction does not promise market acceptance, popularity, or commercial returns.
